name: PrimeBase
tagline: Hamburg-built SQL server popular in pre-press publishing, and parent of the PBXT MySQL engine.
description: PrimeBase started in 1990 as P.INK SQL, one of the first SQL servers for the Macintosh, and was carried on by SNAP Innovation and later PrimeBase Systems GmbH after P.INK's 1995 bankruptcy. The PrimeBase SQL Data Server found its niche in print and pre-press publishing thanks to strong BLOB handling and full-text search, and the team later built PBXT, a log-structured transactional storage engine for MySQL that shipped in MariaDB 5.1 to 5.3. PBXT was dropped from MariaDB 5.5 as unmaintained, and the PrimeBase web sites stopped responding around 2018. It is a historical system; existing installations should plan a migration.
statusNote: PBXT is unmaintained and was dropped from MariaDB 5.5; primebase.org and primebase.com went offline around 2018. Migrate to PostgreSQL or MariaDB.
developer: PrimeBase Systems GmbH (formerly SNAP Innovation, P.INK Software)

pricing.notes: The SQL Data Server was sold commercially; the PBXT storage engine was free GPL software. Neither is offered today.

scale.notes: Single-server deployments with an optional PrimeBase Replication Server.

strengths: Efficient BLOB storage and full-text search tuned for publishing workflows
Ran natively on classic Mac OS long before most SQL servers did
PBXT showed an MVCC, log-structured alternative to InnoDB inside MySQL
weaknesses: Vendor and web sites are gone; no supported downloads
PBXT has known unfixed bugs and is excluded from modern MariaDB
Tiny user base concentrated in one industry
useCases: Supporting or migrating legacy pre-press and publishing systems
Studying PBXT's log-based storage engine design
notIdealFor: Anything needing vendor support or security fixes
